question: Who among the following was an Anglo-Indian teacher of the Hindu college of Calcutta to initiate the Young Bengal Movement?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Henry Vivian Derozio**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Henry Vivian Derozio** was an Anglo-Indian teacher at the Hindu College of Calcutta.
 
• He is known for initiating the **Young Bengal Movement** in the early 19th century.
 
• The movement was characterized by its progressive and radical ideas, advocating for social reforms, freedom of thought, and questioning traditional practices.
 
• Derozio's teachings and ideas greatly influenced his students, who came to be known as "Derozians" or "Young Bengal."
 
• The movement played a significant role in the intellectual and social awakening in Bengal during that period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **David Hare** was a Scottish watchmaker and philanthropist who played a crucial role in the establishment of several educational institutions in Calcutta, including the Hindu College.
 
• **Charles Wilkins** was an English typographer and Orientalist, known for his translation of the Bhagavad Gita into English.
 
• **Henry Colbert** is not associated with the Young Bengal Movement or the Hindu College of Calcutta.
 
• The Hindu College of Calcutta, established in 1817, was one of the earliest institutions of higher education in India and played a pivotal role in the Bengal Renaissance.
